clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. E sta b lish m en t, (a) There is established the Presidential Commis­
sion on Broadcasting to Cuba.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The Commission shall be composed of 11 members appointed by the 
President from among citizens of the United States.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: (c) The President shall designate one of the members to be the Chairman.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) There shall be a three member Executive Committee of the Commission 
which shall be composed of the Chairman and two other members elected by 
the Commission.

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) The Commission shall develop a recommended plan for radio broadcasting 
intended for transmission to Cuba. The purpose of the plan shall be to 
promote open communication of information and ideas to Cuba and in particu­
lar broadcasting to the Cuban people of accurate information about Cuba.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The Commission shall examine issues related to effectively carrying out 
such a plan for radio broadcasting to Cuba. These shall include, but not be 
limited to, possible program content, information gathering, writing and edit­
ing needs, staffing requirements, legal structure for a broadcasting organiza­
tion, proposed legislation, sample budgets, and the location, structure and 
function of possible broadcasting stations.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) The Commission may conduct studies, inquiries, hearings, and meetings as 
it deems necessary. It may assemble and disseminate information, and issue 
reports and other publications. It may also coordinate, sponsor, or oversee 
projects, studies, events and other activities that it deems necessary or 
desirable for development of a recommended program of broadcasting to 
Cuba.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) The Executive Committee may coordinate the work of the Commission and 
may act on behalf of the whole Commission.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) The Commission shall submit its recommendations and final report to the 
President and the Secretary of State no later than October 1,1982.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text: Sec. 3. A d m in istra tio n .

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Members of the Commission who are not otherwise Government employ­
ees shall serve without any compensation for their work on the Commission. 
However, all members shall be entitled to travel expenses, including per diem 
in lieu of subsistence, as authorized by law (5 U.S.C. 5701-5707).

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The heads of Executive agencies shall, to the extent permitted by law, 
provide the Commission such information and advice with respect to radio 
broadcasting to Cuba as the Commission may require for the purpose of 
carrying out its functions.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Expenses of the Commission shall be paid from funds available to the 
Secretary of State.

clauses.text:
(a) Notwithstanding any other Executive order, the functions of the President

EO 12323 (Presidential Commission on Broadcasting to Cuba), signed 1981-09-22. The order establishes the Presidential Commission on Broadcasting to Cuba of eleven members (Section 1), its functions of developing a plan for radio broadcasting to Cuba (Section 2, with the final report due by October 1, 1982), administration (Section 3) and general provisions (Section 4). EO 12366 later raised the membership to twelve. First end: Section 4(b) of the order provides that the Commission shall terminate on October 1, 1982, or 60 days after submitting its final report, whichever is earlier. The fixed date is the latest date on which the Commission could end, so I record 1982-10-01 as the first end by the order's own terms (read inclusively: the Commission exists through October 1, 1982; the exclusive reading would put it at the start of that day). The report-relative alternative could have ended it earlier; the held packet has no dated record of the final report, so that possibility is disclosed and no earlier date is claimed. Section 4(h) of EO 12399 later revoked the order, effective December 31, 1982, which is after the sunset and is a later event.
